fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind the Page
fields.features_subheading: A freelancer landing page with your services, the brief form under them, and the table where every client inquiry lands.
fields.feature_1:
Services and briefs from one prompt

Describe what you sell and what a client must tell you, and Emergent builds the page: the packages, the rates, and the brief form for each. Change a package later by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
Each inquiry saved to a table you own

Every brief from the page lands as a row in a database you own, with the package picked, the budget, and the deadline. Sort by budget to decide which brief gets a reply first.
fields.feature_3:
Rush work reaches you on Slack

Set the turnaround that counts as rush, and the app sends any request under it to Slack or email the moment it arrives. Everything slower waits in the table until you open it.
fields.feature_4:
Quotes worked out from the request

Give the page your rate and the unit you charge by: words, hours, or minutes of footage. The app multiplies the client's number by the rate and shows the quote before they send it.
fields.feature_5:
A web address with your name in it

Put the page on a domain you own, such as yourname.com, so the address on your invoice matches the page a client opens. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Paid plans export the full code of the page, the brief form, and the database to your GitHub repository. Hand it to a developer, or keep hosting it on Emergent as clients come in.

fields.tab_content_1:
Three packages, and a brief form under each

Brona Marwood writes for software companies and sells three packages: a homepage, an email sequence, and a retainer. The brief form under each asks for the deadline, the budget, and a product link. An email sequence brief arrives with a $1,400 budget and a 3-week deadline, saved with its package.
fields.tab_content_2:
He sees any 48-hour rush before the rest

Caspar Askew edits launch videos, and his request form asks each client for a turnaround. Anything under 72 hours is marked rush and sent to him on Slack. This week a 48-hour launch teaser reached him first, while a 6-day product demo and a 10-day tutorial series waited in the table.
fields.tab_content_3:
One upload comes back as a $576 quote

Berit Kallio translates technical manuals from German to English at $0.12 a word. A client uploads the manual on her page, the app reads its word count, and the quote appears before the client sends anything: 4,800 words comes to $576. Each quote is saved with the file and the client's email.
fields.tab_content_4:
October ended with 22 inquiries and 9 booked calls

Lenore Sabel keeps the books for restaurants and gives a visitor one next step: a 20-minute intro call. Each inquiry is saved with the restaurant's name, and the dashboard counts the month as it goes. October closed with 22 inquiries, and 9 became booked calls, the last from Cedar Spoon Diner.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Freelancer Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a freelancer landing page around your services and test its brief form before a client sees it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what a brief must answer
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Choose what reaches you at once
fields.howto_step_1_des: List each service as a package a client can pick, with what it includes, how long it takes, and a starting price. A short set of packages is easier to choose from than a long menu, and each one gets its own brief form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the questions you would ask on a first call: when the work is due, what the client can spend, and where to see the product. Keep it to four or five, and offer the budget as ranges so a client is not guessing at one number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent the services, the questions, and who the page is for, in plain sentences. Emergent builds the page and the database table behind it, and you change any part of it later by writing another prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the inquiries that should not wait, such as a budget over $2,000, and where each one goes: Slack or email. Everything else stays in the table, where you can sort it by deadline when you sit down to reply.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add two or three short client quotes next to the packages they bought, with the client's name and role. A quote about a homepage rewrite belongs beside the homepage package, where a visitor is deciding whether to send a brief.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Move the page to your domain
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect a domain you own, so the page address matches the one on your email and invoices. Then open the finished page on a phone and on a laptop, since a client may read it on either before sending a brief.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in every brief form with a realistic request and check the row it creates in the table. When each package saves correctly, put the link in your email signature and at the top of every proposal you send.

faq_plan.q: What is a freelancer landing page?
faq_plan.a: A freelancer landing page is a single page that sells one person's services and asks a visitor to take one step, such as sending a brief or booking a call. It says what you do and for whom, shows where pricing starts, and collects the details you need to reply.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a freelancer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe your services and the questions a new client should answer, and Emergent's AI landing page builder builds it with a form under each service and a table that stores every reply. Read the draft, ask for changes in plain words, then publish it. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should a freelancer landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Include one line on the work you do and the clients you do it for, your services as packages with a starting price, a few client quotes, and one form or booking step. Leave out anything that pulls a visitor away from that step, such as a blog feed or a long work history.

faq_plan.q: Should a freelancer landing page focus on me or on my services?
faq_plan.a: Lead with the services, because a client arrives with a job to fill and wants to see whether you do it. A short line about you and a photo help, but the page is about the work. If the goal is to introduce yourself rather than sell a service, a personal landing page fits better.

faq_plan.q: Should a freelancer landing page list package prices?
faq_plan.a: Show a starting price for each package when your work is priced in a way you can state, such as per project or per word. A starting price turns away briefs that cannot meet it. For custom work, ask for a budget range in the brief form instead. On a page built with Emergent, that range is saved with each brief in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should the brief form on a freelancer landing page ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask what the project is, when it is due, the budget range, and where you can see the client's product or brand. Add one question specific to your trade, such as word count for a translator or video length for an editor. Save everything else for the first call.

faq_plan.q: Can I use a freelancer landing page as the link in my social media bio?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A freelancer landing page works as the one link in a social profile, because it takes a visitor straight to your services and a brief form. If you need several links in one place, such as a shop, a podcast, and a newsletter, a link in bio landing page is built for that.

faq_plan.q: Is one freelancer landing page enough, or do I need a full website?
faq_plan.a: One landing page is enough when you sell one kind of service and every visitor should take the same step. A full website starts to make sense once you need separate pages for several services, a blog, or long case studies. You can start with the page and add pages to the same app later by prompting Emergent.

faq_plan.q: How do I get testimonials for a freelancer landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask each client within a week of delivering, while the result is fresh, and request one specific sentence about what changed after your work. Get written permission to publish their name and role. A quote that names the result, such as a launch date met, tells a visitor more than general praise.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a freelancer landing page and a portfolio?
faq_plan.a: A freelancer landing page sells services, with packages, prices, and a brief form as the main step, while a portfolio lets finished work do the selling. If clients pick you by your past projects, start with a portfolio landing page and link to it from your service page.

plan.angle: Searchers for freelancer landing page want a page that turns a visitor into client work, and the ranking results are template galleries that stop at the design. This page follows the inquiry instead: four freelancers whose single page sells a service and lands every brief, rush request, instant quote and booked call in a table they own. It stays off sibling ground: no work galleries (portfolio), no about-me pages (personal), no link menus (link in bio), no job applications (resume). The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what to include, page versus full website, showing rates, brief form questions, link in bio use, length, testimonials and how it differs from a portfolio.
